claims.note: licence: Public domain; supersedes a rights-unknown image on rights

image_measured.measured_from: the downloaded file's own header, never the API's report

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).

values.value: Johnson was born on September 30, 1896, in East Boston, Massachusetts
He played football for Everett High School in Everett, Massachusetts

He was a part of the 1914 Everett team that went 13–0 and outscored opponents 600 to 0. In the national championship of high school football, Everett, the best team in the East, was matched against Oak Park High School from Illinois, the best team in the West
Everett defeated Oak Park 80 to 0. Johnson went on to play tackle at Washington and Lee University
After his football career, Johnson worked for many years in the public relations department of the Hiram Walker & Sons Ltd. in Boston
He resided in Belmont, Massachusetts, and later in Laconia, New Hampshire. Johnson died on November 6, 1985, at a nursing home in Meredith, New Hampshire
==Football career== In 1917, Johnson played with the Massillon Tigers of the Ohio League, where he received all-pro honors in 1917. He was also World War I Army veteran and Purple Heart recipient

bio.value: Jim Thorpe's career, eight seasons in the APFA from 1920, began with the Canton Bulldogs. He played for six clubs: the Canton Bulldogs, the Cleveland Indians, the Oorang Indians, the Rock Island Independents, the New York Giants and the Chicago Cardinals. He did not play in 1927. He was later Head Coach of the Oorang Indians from 1922 to 1923. He was a head coach at two other clubs too. In all he scored 51 points over five seasons. He died on March 28, 1953, in Lomita, CA.

values.value: Bacon was married in December 1920 to Ruth Weaver of Ponca City, Oklahoma.{{cite news|title=Weds Ponca, Okla

Bacon United in Marriage to Miss Ruth Weaver|newspaper=The South Bend Tribune|date=December 23, 1920|page=18|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/76727099/marriage-of-bacon-weaver/|via=Newspapers.com}} Bacon died in 1977 in Sandusky, Ohio

==Military service== When the United States entered World War I, Bacon began studying wireless telegraphy and signalling in anticipation of joining the Aviation Corps. He was one of only two young men out of 500 who passed the eight-hour examination for the Aviation Corps
and was ordered to report for active duty one week after graduating from Wabash

==Professional baseball and football== Prior to the creation of the National Football League (NFL), he played professional football for the Pine Village Athletic Club in 1917 and the Hammond Clabbys in 1918. He also played professional baseball in the Three-I and Central Leagues, probably in 1917

He also worked for the Dayton Engineering Laboratories Co. (Delco) as the head of educational development. When the NFL was formed in 1920, the Triangles were one of the original participants. On October 3, 1920, the Triangles defeated the Columbus Panhandles, 14–0, in the first official NFL game with Bacon as the starting right halfback
Fullback Lou Partlow gained fame for scoring the first NFL touchdown in the third quarter, and Bacon followed in the fourth quarter with the first NFL punt return for a touchdown
He also played for the Akron Pros in 1923. He appeared in 47 NFL games, playing at halfback, fullback and end, scored 14 touchdowns, and kicked two extra points

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).

values.value: Louis was the seventh child (of eleven) born to Adam Granville Partlow (1857–1928) and Amanda Isabell Muirhead (1864–1947)
His siblings: Clara, George, William Jesse, Gussie, Mary, Frank, Vernie (who died in early childhood), Madge, Violet and Dorothy
She was the daughter of John Henry Myers and Mary Hipple
The family lived in Ohio for many years, but in the 1950s Lou and Ruth moved to California
This is where they lived out the rest of their long lives, and are buried
Lou died at the age of 88, and Ruth at the age of 86
They are buried at Forest Lawn Memorial Park, Hollywood Hills

Partlow also played with the Cincinnati Celts before joining the Dayton Gym-Cadets in 1915, the year before they changed their name to the Dayton Triangles. On 3 October 1920, the Dayton Triangles beat the Columbus Panhandles 14–0 in the first ever NFL game, in which Partlow scored the first touchdown

bio.value: Guy Chamberlin scored 42 points for the Canton Bulldogs in 1922; only three men in the NFL scored more that season. Over eight seasons he played for six clubs: the Decatur Staleys (later the Staleys), the Chicago Staleys, the Canton Bulldogs, the Cleveland Bulldogs, the Frankford Yellow Jackets and the Chicago Cardinals. He came back as Head Coach of the Frankford Yellow Jackets from 1925 to 1926. He was a head coach at three other clubs too. He died on April 4, 1967, in Lincoln, NE.

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).

Chamberlin was born in Blue Springs, Nebraska, in 1894. He was raised with five siblings on a family farm in Blue Springs
He graduated from Blue Springs High School in 1911

He returned to the Nebraska Wesleyan football team in the fall of 1912 and was again selected as an all-state player. In announcing its selection of Chamberlin to the all-state team, the Omaha World-Herald wrote: "Chamberlin is almost in a class by himself. He is a fierce and aggressive runner and adopts the system of bowling over the opposing tacklers in much the same style as the famous Coy of Y

After leading the Cornhuskers to a 20–19 victory over Notre Dame, The Omaha World-Herald wrote of Chamberlin: "His defensive stunts bordered upon the miraculous, while his open field running, in which he displayed that famous 'side walk trot' to the best advantage, brought victory to the colors of the Cornhuskers." In his final game for Nebraska, Chamberlin scored four touchdowns, including a 60-y

==1916–1919== ===Farmer and coach at Doane College=== After graduating from Nebraska, Chamberlin returned to the family farm. In August 1916, he was hired as the athletic director and football coach at Doane College in Crete, Nebraska

Draft registration card dated June 1917 for Berlin Guy Chamberlin, born January 16, 1894, working as a farmer in the employ of Elmer Chamberlin. Registration State: Nebraska; Registration County: Gage; Roll: 1711529. Source Information: Ancestry.com. U.S., World War I Draft Registration Cards, 1917-1918 [database on-line]

==Professional football== ===Canton Bulldogs=== Chamberlin began playing professional football in 1919 as an end for Jim Thorpe's undefeated 1919 Canton Bulldogs, winners of that year's unofficial professional football championship with a 9–0–1 record. ===Decatur/Chicago Staleys=== In August 1920, the American Professional Football Association (APFA, later renamed the National Football League) was
===Canton/Cleveland Bulldogs=== In 1922, Chamberlin joined the Canton Bulldogs in multiple roles as a player, head coach, team captain, and part owner. (part owner)
He played at the halfback position in the first game of the season and at end for the remaining 12 games; he reportedly "played every minute of the thirteen games."

Dave Noble, who played for the 1924 Bulldogs, explained Chamberlin's coaching success as follows: "Guy Chamberlain knows as much or more football than any other coach in the country. Moreover, he has a faculty for getting the most out of players, not because he is a driver, for he isn't that sort, but because they like him and will do their utmost to please him by playing hard."

Chamberlin returned to the lineup in mid-December and led the team to victories in its final two games. In 1926, Chamberlin returned to Philadelphia and appeared in all 17 games as a player, despite being the oldest player on the team at age 32. He led the 1926 Yellow Jackets to an NFL championship with a 14–1–2 record, shutting out 10 NFL opponents and outscoring all NFL opponents, 236 to 49
though contemporary accounts do not corroborate the claim
===Chicago Cardinals=== In August 1927, Chamberlin signed as player/coach for the Chicago Cardinals

Chamberlin has the best win percentage ( ) of any coach in NFL history with a minimum of 50 games. See List of National Football League head coaches with 50 wins. His accomplishment of winning a championship with three separate franchises in a major North American sports league would not be matched until 1997, when Scotty Bowman won the 1997 Stanley Cup Finals. Author Chris Willis ranks Chamberlin
*In 1967, the University of Nebraska began awarding the Guy Chamberlin Trophy. It is awarded each year to the player "who has the qualities and dedication of the Husker Tradition."
*In 2017, his jersey was retired by the University of Nebraska and his name was added to the north facade of Memorial Stadium

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. bio.value: Starting with the Kansas City Blues (later the Cowboys) in 1924, Steve Owen played ten seasons through 1934. From there he went to the Cleveland Bulldogs in 1925 and the New York Giants in 1926–31 and 1933–34. He did not play in 1932. He came back as Head Coach of the New York Giants from 1931 to 1953. He spent another three seasons as an assistant and was a head coach at four other clubs too. He died on May 17, 1964, in Oneida, NY.

bio.value: Dutch Clark scored 73 points for the Detroit Lions in 1936; only one man in the NFL scored more that season. His seven seasons were with the Portsmouth Spartans from 1931 to 1932 and the Detroit Lions from 1934 to 1938. He did not play in 1933. He was later Head Coach of the Cleveland Rams from 1939 to 1942. He spent another one season as an assistant and was a head coach at two other clubs too. In all he ran for 2,772 yards over six seasons. He died on August 5, 1978, in Canon City, CO.

bio.value: In 1926, playing for the New York Giants, Hinkey Haines scored 36 points — only nine men in the NFL scored more that season. He played seven seasons: for the Frankford Yellow Jackets in 1923, the New York Giants from 1925 to 1928 and the Staten Island Stapletons in 1929 and 1931. He was in and out of the game, missing 1924 and 1930. He later became Head Coach of the Staten Island Stapletons in 1931. Over five seasons he scored 132 points. He was a United States Army veteran.

bio.value: Dutch Hendrian played three seasons in the NFL, 1923 to 1925, starting with the Akron Pros. He went on to four more clubs: the Canton Bulldogs, the Green Bay Packers, the New York Giants and the Rock Island Independents. He later became Head Coach of the Akron Pros in 1923. In all he scored 50 points over four seasons. He died on December 13, 1953, in Los Angeles, CA.

bio.value: Starting with the Canton Bulldogs in 1922, Link Lyman played eleven seasons through 1934. He played for four clubs: the Canton Bulldogs, the Cleveland Bulldogs, the Frankford Yellow Jackets and the Chicago Bears. He was in and out of the game, missing 1929 and 1932. Over three seasons he scored 37 points. He died on December 28, 1972, in Barstow, CA.

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).

Over six seasons he played for four clubs: the Canton Bulldogs, the Cleveland Bulldogs, the Frankford Yellow Jackets and the Chicago Cardinals. He later became Head Coach of the Chicago Cardinals in 1927. Over six seasons he scored 151 points. He was a United States Marine Corps veteran.

image_measured.measured_from: the downloaded file's own header, never the API's report

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).

bio.value: Cal Hubbard played nine seasons, 1927 to 1936, starting with the New York Giants. He played for the New York Giants in 1927–28 and 1936, the Green Bay Packers in 1929–33 and 1935 and the Pittsburgh Pirates in 1936. He did not play in 1934. He later coached, as Offensive Line of the Green Bay Packers in 1935. He died on October 17, 1977, in St. Petersburg, FL.

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).

extra._portrait_usability_why: Dimensions overstate portrait usability for full-body and group shots. Al Bedner at 447px is a sharp full-length 1918 photograph whose FACE is roughly 60px -- worse as a page portrait than a clean 240px headshot. The usable quantity is the face region and the face region is NOT measured here. A >=200px count is a floor, not a promise, and nothing downstream may read it as one. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.

supersedes._rule: A rights-clear photograph supersedes a rights-UNKNOWN one on rights alone, whatever their sizes. RULED 2026-09-07 by Ryan.
supersedes._kept: The superseded photograph's claim is NEVER deleted or rewritten. The new claim names it in `supersedes`, and the old one stays readable. The archive says what it held and why it stopped preferring it -- consistent with DISAGREEMENTS_ARE_HELD, and it keeps this ingest out of build files it does not own (photos.json is the PSF set's, not this run's).
